# LIGHTSPEED receiver 046D:C547 ("USB Receiver") with a PRO X Superlight on
# slot 1, over a whole run: arrival with the mouse off, the mouse switched on,
# 43 min without traffic (the PC sleeps for the last minute), resume, then the
# mouse switched off and on.
#
# Real capture: owner capture 2026-11-23, G HUB closed; one
# process ran both recorded sessions, so the first part equals
# c547-superlight-arrival.txt. The trace also held the headset dongle; only
# this group's frames are kept (collections FF00:0001 short and FF00:0002
# long), verbatim, except the mouse's unit id in the 0x0003 fn 0 reply,
# replaced by the synthetic 1A2B3C4D. The resume notification is not in the
# trace: `resume` stands where its read was written. The trailing `# +<s>` is
# the frame's time in the capture, counted from app start.
#
# Format: `out <short|long> <hex>` is a frame BatterySight writes, `in` one it
# reads, `@t+<ms>` lets time pass and ticks the hub, `resume` is the system
# resume notification. Each `in` and `resume` advances the clock by 1 ms; `@t+`
# lines restore the capture's gaps over 100 ms. The `out` lines after an input
# are the writes that input causes.

# Group arrival: notification flags already on; ask for every paired slot.
out short 10 FF 81 00 00 00 00  # +0.006 s
in  short 10 FF 81 00 00 01 00  # +0.008 s
out short 10 FF 80 02 02 00 00  # +0.009 s
# Slot 1, link not established (0x41 byte 4 = 0x62): nothing asked.
in  short 10 01 41 11 62 93 40  # +0.011 s
in  short 10 FF 80 02 00 00 00  # +0.012 s
# Mouse switched on: link established (0xA2) -> ping slot 1 -> discovery.
@t+30167

# 43 min without a frame in either direction; the PC sleeps from +2600.7 s.

@t+729

in  short 10 01 41 11 62 93 40  # +2657.580 s
# The mouse's battery broadcast (80 %) comes after the link-lost 0x41: a push
# is a sign of life, so the mouse is awake again for the scheduler.
in  long  11 01 06 00 50 08 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00  # +2657.583 s
# Resume: one read per awake device, so slot 1 is read. The receiver answers
# itself (no radio traffic) with HID++ 1.0 error 0x08 -> asleep.
@t+140
